title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
shortDescription: On-board charger module has commanded the MIL on due to an internal fault.
fullDescription:
P0D00 is set when the On-Board Charger (OBC) control module reports a fault severe enough to require MIL illumination. The OBC handles AC-to-DC conversion to charge the high-voltage traction battery from a Level 1 or Level 2 EVSE.

This is an umbrella code; subordinate P0Dxx codes typically accompany it and pinpoint the specific failure (input voltage, output voltage, isolation, communication, etc.).

Pull all stored codes from the OBC, hybrid control module, and battery ECU before any repair to avoid replacing the wrong module.
safetyImpact: Vehicle may refuse to charge; reduced range. High-voltage faults are inherently dangerous and require trained service.

causes.cause: Subordinate P0Dxx fault not yet repaired

fixSteps.title: Scan all modules
fixSteps.instruction: Use a hybrid-capable scan tool to read all stored codes from OBC, HCM, BECM. Address subordinate codes first.

fixSteps.title: Inspect HV interlock loop
fixSteps.instruction: Verify all orange HV connectors are seated and service disconnect lever is engaged.

fixSteps.title: Replace OBC if isolated
fixSteps.instruction: If subordinate codes are cleared and P0D00 persists, replace the on-board charger and program per OEM procedure.

faq.a: Yes for a hybrid until pack depletes; for a BEV you cannot recharge until repaired.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Control Module General Fault
shortDescription: On-board charger reports a non-specific internal fault.
fullDescription:
P0D01 indicates the OBC has run a self-test and detected an internal anomaly that does not map to a more specific code. Common triggers include MCU watchdog resets, gate-driver fault flags, and bus voltage transients during plug-in.

Intermittent P0D01 events are often caused by poor EVSE quality (unstable AC supply, ground loops). Persistent P0D01 usually means the OBC needs replacement.
safetyImpact: Charging disabled. Possible HV system isolation event.
symptoms: EVSE clicks but no current flows

fixSteps.title: Try a different EVSE
fixSteps.instruction: Plug into a known-good Level 2 unit on a separate circuit to rule out supply-side issues.

fixSteps.title: Check AC supply quality
fixSteps.instruction: Verify line voltage, ground continuity, and absence of GFCI nuisance trips.

fixSteps.title: Replace OBC
fixSteps.instruction: If supply is clean and code persists, replace charger.

faq.a: Often not; DCFC bypasses the OBC. Test to confirm OBC vs charge-port wiring.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Control Module Internal Performance
shortDescription: OBC efficiency or output performance below expected threshold.
fullDescription:
P0D02 sets when measured OBC output power is significantly below commanded value, or efficiency is below spec. Typically indicates aging power semiconductors, dried thermal interface material, or partial gate-driver failure.

The vehicle may still charge but at a reduced rate, and the OBC may run hotter than normal.
safetyImpact: Slow charging; potential thermal stress on OBC.

causes.cause: Dried thermal paste / coolant flow loss

fixSteps.title: Verify coolant flow
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the HV coolant pump runs during charging and the OBC loop is bled.

fixSteps.title: Replace OBC
fixSteps.instruction: If thermal management is OK, replace the charger.

faq.a: Some OEMs issue OBC firmware updates that improve performance; check for TSBs first.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Input Voltage Out of Range
shortDescription: OBC sees AC input voltage above or below expected range.
fullDescription:
P0D03 indicates the OBC measured AC line voltage outside its acceptable window (typically 85-265 VAC for global chargers). Causes include bad EVSE, poor outlet wiring, undervoltage events, or shared circuits with heavy loads.

This code rarely indicates an OBC failure; investigate the supply side first.
safetyImpact: Charging stops. No mobility loss for hybrids.

fixSteps.title: Measure outlet voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Verify 120V/240V at the outlet under load with a DMM.

fixSteps.title: Try alternate circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Plug into a different breaker known to be in good condition.

fixSteps.title: Replace EVSE
fixSteps.instruction: If supply is OK, swap the charging cable.

faq.a: Only with a clean sine-wave inverter generator and proper grounding.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Input Voltage Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: AC input voltage sensor circuit fault.
fullDescription: P0D04 sets when the OBC's internal AC input voltage sense circuit fails plausibility checks (e.g., reads 0 V while current is flowing, or reads non-zero with no AC connected). Indicates an internal sensor or analog front-end fault.

fixSteps.title: Verify with second EVSE
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm fault is OBC-side by trying a known good EVSE.

fixSteps.title: Replace OBC
fixSteps.instruction: Sense circuit is internal and not field-serviceable.

faq.a: 12V reset may temporarily clear but code returns once charging is attempted.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Input Voltage Sensor Circuit Low
shortDescription: AC input voltage sensor reads abnormally low.
fullDescription: P0D05 indicates the input voltage sense circuit is reading a value lower than physically possible given charging activity. Usually a shorted sensing resistor or open trace on the OBC analog board.

fixSteps.title: Confirm fault
fixSteps.instruction: Read live data; expected value is 0V before plug-in, line voltage during charging.

fixSteps.title: Replace OBC
fixSteps.instruction: Internal repair impractical.

faq.a: No; this is a hardware sensor failure.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Input Voltage Sensor Circuit High
shortDescription: AC input voltage sensor reads abnormally high.
fullDescription: P0D06 sets when the input voltage sensing reports a value above the physically reasonable maximum. Often indicates a shorted reference rail or sensor IC failure inside the OBC.

fixSteps.title: Confirm with scan tool
fixSteps.instruction: Compare measured input voltage in live data versus actual outlet voltage.

fixSteps.title: Replace OBC
fixSteps.instruction: Replace charger; sensor is internal.

faq.a: No; isolated to OBC analog front-end.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Input Voltage Sensor Circuit Intermittent
shortDescription: Intermittent fault in AC input voltage sensing.
fullDescription: P0D07 is set on intermittent dropouts of the input voltage sense signal. Usually due to cold-solder joints, marginal sensor IC, or vibration-induced contact issues inside the OBC.

fixSteps.title: Capture freeze frame
fixSteps.instruction: Note ambient temperature and SOC at fault.

fixSteps.title: Replace OBC
fixSteps.instruction: Intermittent OBC analog faults are not field-serviceable.

faq.a: Several OEMs have TSBs for early OBC PCBs; check by VIN.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Input Voltage Above Maximum
shortDescription: AC line voltage exceeds OBC safe maximum.
fullDescription:
P0D08 sets when measured AC supply voltage is above the OBC's safe operating maximum (typically 265 VAC). Most common cause is mis-wired 240V outlet wired with two hots from different phases of a 480V supply, or a generator producing overvoltage.

Do not continue to charge until the supply is corrected; sustained overvoltage can damage the OBC.
safetyImpact: Risk of OBC damage and fire if uncorrected.

fixSteps.title: Measure outlet voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm L1-L2 is ~240 VAC and L1-N / L2-N are ~120 VAC.

fixSteps.title: Have electrician correct wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Outlet must be on a proper single-phase 240V circuit.

faq.a: Possibly. Have OBC checked if charging does not resume after wiring fix.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Input Voltage Below Minimum
shortDescription: AC line voltage below OBC operational minimum.
fullDescription: P0D09 indicates measured AC supply voltage is below the minimum required by the OBC (often 85 VAC). Causes include long extension cords, brownouts, undersized circuits, and shared loads.
safetyImpact: Charging will not start; no mobility loss for hybrids.

causes.cause: Voltage drop on long extension cord

fixSteps.title: Eliminate extension cord
fixSteps.instruction: Plug Level 1 EVSE directly into a wall outlet.

fixSteps.title: Reduce shared loads
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure no other appliances on the same circuit.

faq.a: Not recommended; install a proper circuit instead.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Input Current Out of Range
shortDescription: AC input current outside expected envelope.
fullDescription: P0D0A sets when the OBC measures input current that does not match commanded current (e.g., commands 16 A but measures 8 A or 25 A). Indicates either an internal current-sensor fault or an unexpected supply impedance.

causes.cause: EVSE reporting incorrect pilot duty cycle

symptoms: Charge slower than commanded or fault

fixSteps.title: Try alternate EVSE
fixSteps.instruction: Rule out EVSE pilot signal issues.

fixSteps.title: Replace OBC
fixSteps.instruction: If problem follows the car, replace charger.

faq.a: An oscilloscope on the J1772 pilot can confirm EVSE behavior.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Input Current Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: AC input current sensor circuit fault.
fullDescription: P0D0B is set on circuit-level fault in the input current sensor (usually a Hall-effect device on the AC input lines). The OBC cannot measure or limit input current safely without it and refuses to charge.

fixSteps.title: Read live data
fixSteps.instruction: Verify input current PID is implausible (stuck at 0 or rail).

fixSteps.title: Replace OBC
fixSteps.instruction: Sensor is internal to charger.

faq.q: Any way to defeat the inhibit?
faq.a: No, and you should not; uncontrolled current can start a fire.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Output Voltage Out of Range
shortDescription: OBC HV output voltage outside expected window.
fullDescription: P0D10 sets when DC output voltage from the OBC is outside the expected range relative to commanded value and HV battery voltage. Could be OBC power-stage fault or HV contactor / battery-side issue.
safetyImpact: Charging disabled. May indicate HV pack fault.

fixSteps.title: Verify contactor closure
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm HV contactors close on charge request.

fixSteps.title: Measure HV bus
fixSteps.instruction: With proper PPE, verify pack voltage matches BECM report.

fixSteps.title: Replace OBC
fixSteps.instruction: If pack and contactors are healthy, replace charger.

faq.a: PHEVs can run on engine; BEVs cannot recharge.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Output Voltage Sensor Circuit Low
shortDescription: OBC output voltage sensor reads abnormally low.
fullDescription: P0D11 sets when the DC output voltage sense circuit reports an implausibly low value. Indicates internal sensor or analog front-end fault.

fixSteps.title: Confirm fault
fixSteps.instruction: Compare OBC output PID to BECM voltage at charge initiation.

fixSteps.title: Replace OBC
fixSteps.instruction: Internal sensor; replace charger.

faq.a: Unlikely; OBC inhibits before output reaches pack.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Output Voltage Sensor Circuit High
shortDescription: OBC output voltage sensor reads abnormally high.
fullDescription: P0D12 sets on implausibly high readings from the DC output voltage sensor. Either a broken reference path or a true overvoltage event detected. Either way, the OBC inhibits charging until cleared.

fixSteps.title: Inspect freeze frame
fixSteps.instruction: If overvoltage was real, BECM should show corresponding event.

fixSteps.title: Replace OBC
fixSteps.instruction: Replace charger and verify with controlled charge cycle.

faq.a: Only if BECM logged actual cell overvoltage events.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Output Current Out of Range
shortDescription: OBC DC output current outside expected envelope.
fullDescription: P0D14 indicates OBC output current does not match commanded value. Can result from OBC power-stage limitation, thermal derating not reported, or output sensor drift.

fixSteps.title: Verify thermal headroom
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm OBC coolant flow and ambient temps.

fixSteps.title: Replace OBC
fixSteps.instruction: If thermal management is OK, replace charger.

faq.a: Some OEMs update OBC current limits via reflash; check TSBs.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Output Current Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: DC output current sensor circuit fault.
fullDescription: P0D15 sets when the OBC's DC output current sensor fails plausibility checks. Without this measurement, the OBC cannot regulate charging current safely.

fixSteps.title: Read PIDs
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm output current is stuck or implausible.

fixSteps.title: Replace OBC
fixSteps.instruction: Replace charger.

faq.a: BECM has its own; both must agree for charging to proceed.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: OBC internal temperature sensor fault.
fullDescription: P0D20 sets when the OBC's internal NTC temperature sensor (typically mounted to the heatsink) reports out-of-range or open/short values. Without this signal, the OBC cannot thermal-derate and inhibits charging as a safety measure.

fixSteps.title: Check temp PID
fixSteps.instruction: Compare OBC reported temp to ambient at cold start.

fixSteps.title: Replace OBC
fixSteps.instruction: Internal sensor.

faq.a: OBC inhibits charging precisely to prevent that.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Over Temperature
shortDescription: OBC heatsink temperature exceeded thermal limit.
fullDescription: P0D21 sets when OBC heatsink temperature exceeds the safe limit, often during sustained Level 2 charging in hot conditions or with degraded cooling. The OBC will derate or stop charging until temperature drops.
symptoms: Charging slows or stops in hot weather

fixSteps.title: Check coolant level
fixSteps.instruction: Verify HV coolant reservoir is at MAX.

fixSteps.title: Bleed cooling loop
fixSteps.instruction: Run dealer-procedure bleed; air pockets are common.

fixSteps.title: Test pump and radiator
fixSteps.instruction: Verify pump runs on charge and radiator is unobstructed.

faq.a: Level 1 charging produces less heat and may complete without faulting.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Cooling System Performance
shortDescription: OBC cooling system performance below threshold.
fullDescription: P0D22 sets when expected coolant temperature drop across the OBC is not observed during charging. Indicates pump weak, low flow, or temperature sensor mismatch.

fixSteps.title: Pump test
fixSteps.instruction: Command pump on with bidirectional control; verify flow.

fixSteps.title: Replace pump if weak
fixSteps.instruction: Replace HV coolant pump and bleed system.

faq.a: Usually a separate low-conductivity loop; do not mix.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Communication Lost
shortDescription: Communication with OBC lost on HS-CAN.
fullDescription: P0D24 sets when other modules can no longer communicate with the OBC over the high-voltage / hybrid CAN bus. Often a wake-up issue, lost 12V supply, or terminator fault rather than an OBC failure.

fixSteps.title: Check 12V to OBC
fixSteps.instruction: Verify fuse and 12V supply at OBC connector.

fixSteps.title: CAN integrity test
fixSteps.instruction: Measure 60 ohms between CAN H/L with key off.

fixSteps.title: Replace OBC if isolated
fixSteps.instruction: If supply and bus are healthy, replace charger.

faq.a: Yes, U0293 typically accompanies P0D24.

title: Hybrid/EV Charge Port Lock Actuator Circuit
shortDescription: Charge port lock actuator circuit fault.
fullDescription: P0D28 sets when the charge-port locking solenoid circuit is open or shorted. Without functioning lock, the OBC refuses to charge to prevent unplugging under load (which could cause arcing).

fixSteps.title: Test actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Bidirectional command lock/unlock with scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check for damage near charge port.

fixSteps.title: Replace actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Often integrated with charge-port assembly.

faq.a: Most EVs have a mechanical emergency release in the trunk or near port.

title: Hybrid/EV Charge Port Lock Actuator Position Implausible
shortDescription: Charge port lock did not reach commanded position.
fullDescription: P0D29 sets when the lock actuator is commanded to engage or disengage but the position feedback sensor disagrees. Often a debris-jammed lock pin or a worn return spring.

fixSteps.title: Clean charge port
fixSteps.instruction: Remove debris; inspect lock pin freedom.

fixSteps.title: Replace charge port assembly
fixSteps.instruction: If pin is worn, replace the assembly.

faq.a: Yes; warm the port and retry before replacing parts.

title: Hybrid/EV Charge Port Pilot (Control Pilot) Circuit
shortDescription: J1772/CCS Control Pilot signal fault.
fullDescription: P0D2A sets when the OBC cannot properly read the EVSE Control Pilot signal (a 1 kHz PWM on pin 5 of J1772 or analogous on CCS/Type 2). Causes include damaged port pin, water ingress, or OBC pilot interface failure.

fixSteps.title: Inspect port pins
fixSteps.instruction: Look for bent, burned, or corroded pins.

fixSteps.title: Test pilot with adapter
fixSteps.instruction: Use J1772 break-out tool or scope to confirm pilot signal at port.

fixSteps.title: Replace port or OBC
fixSteps.instruction: Most often the port assembly; OBC last resort.

faq.a: J1772 pilot break-out testers are widely available.

title: Hybrid/EV Charge Port Proximity Pilot Circuit
shortDescription: J1772/CCS Proximity Pilot signal fault.
fullDescription: P0D2B sets when the proximity pilot signal (used by the car to detect that a connector is plugged in and read connector current capacity) is missing or out of range. The car will not enable charging without proximity confirmation.

fixSteps.title: Try second plug
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm fault is on the car side using a different EVSE.

fixSteps.title: Inspect proximity pin
fixSteps.instruction: Look for bent or burned proximity pin in port.

fixSteps.title: Replace charge port
fixSteps.instruction: Replace assembly if pin is damaged.

faq.a: Tesla cars use proprietary signaling; refer to NACS-specific equivalents.

title: Hybrid/EV DC Fast Charge Contactor Stuck Closed
shortDescription: DCFC contactor welded or stuck closed.
fullDescription:
P0D30 sets when the DC fast-charge contactor is commanded open but voltage feedback shows it remains closed. This is a serious safety condition because the HV bus could remain energized through the charge port.

Vehicle will refuse to drive or charge until the contactor is replaced.
safetyImpact: Severe. HV exposure risk if charge port were unlocked. Requires immediate professional service.

fixSteps.title: Tow to dealer
fixSteps.instruction: Do not attempt DIY; HV exposure risk.

fixSteps.title: Replace contactor and inspect bus
fixSteps.instruction: Often requires PDU/junction-box service.

faq.a: A stuck contactor leaves HV present where it should not be.

title: Hybrid/EV DC Fast Charge Contactor Stuck Open
shortDescription: DCFC contactor will not close on command.
fullDescription: P0D31 sets when the DC fast-charge contactor is commanded closed but feedback shows it remains open. The car will refuse DC fast charging; AC charging via OBC may still work.

fixSteps.title: Check coil resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Per OEM spec at the BECM connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace contactor
fixSteps.instruction: Inside HV junction box; HV-safe procedure.

faq.a: Yes if you have a Level 2 EVSE; trip planning will need adjustment.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Isolation Fault
shortDescription: OBC detects loss of HV-to-chassis isolation.
fullDescription:
P0D40 sets when the OBC's isolation monitor detects a leakage path between the HV bus and chassis ground above the safety threshold (typically 100-500 ohm/V). Possible causes range from moisture ingress to component-level insulation failure.

This is a safety-critical fault; the OBC will inhibit charging and may trigger ready-mode inhibit.
safetyImpact: Severe. Possible HV exposure to chassis. Service immediately.

causes.cause: Moisture in OBC or HV harness

fixSteps.title: Read isolation resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Use OEM scan tool to read live isolation values from BECM.

fixSteps.title: Sectionalize HV components
fixSteps.instruction: Isolate each HV component to find leaking source.

fixSteps.title: Replace faulty component
fixSteps.instruction: Often AC compressor, OBC, or harness.

faq.a: Do not. Tow to a qualified hybrid service shop.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Isolation Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: Isolation sensor circuit fault inside OBC.
fullDescription: P0D41 sets when the isolation monitoring circuit itself returns implausible values. The OBC cannot trust isolation measurements and conservatively inhibits charging.

fixSteps.title: Read freeze frame
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm sensor reading is implausible.

fixSteps.title: Replace OBC
fixSteps.instruction: Sensor is internal.

faq.a: P0D40 is real leakage; P0D41 is the sensor itself failing.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Charger Calibration Not Programmed
shortDescription: OBC calibration data missing or invalid.
fullDescription:
P0D50 sets when the OBC powers up and finds no valid calibration in EEPROM. Common after replacement without programming, after a failed reflash, or after EEPROM corruption.

Car will refuse to charge until OBC is programmed with VIN-specific calibration.

fixSteps.title: Program OBC
fixSteps.instruction: Use OEM scan tool with current calibration file matching VIN.

fixSteps.title: Re-attempt reflash
fixSteps.instruction: If reflash failed, retry with stable 12V and ignition on.

faq.a: OBC programming usually requires OEM tooling.
